newsitem.title: USA: CBOT chairman says CFTC clears him in wheat probe.
newsitem.headline: CBOT chairman says CFTC clears him in wheat probe.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade chairman Patrick Arbor said Thursday the Commodity Futures Trading Commission has cleared him of any wrongdoing in the volatile expiration of the March wheat contract last year.

"I have been informed by the chair of the CFTC that the agency has officially closed its inquiry of my personal trading surrounding the March wheat expiration and will take no further action on the matter," Arbor said in a statement Thursday at the annual Futures Industry Association conference here.
A CBOT official quoted a February CFTC letter as saying, "The commission has not made any finding that your activities constitued a violation."
Arbor said he was "disappointed" with the CFTC for allowing a routine inquiry into his personal trading records to be made public.

"Throughout my career, my trading practices have been beyond reproach and I really am disappointed that the CFTC allowed a standard inquiry, which resulted in nothing, to end up in the media," Arbor said.
"I hope the agency is taking steps to ensure that similar incidents will be prevented," Arbor said.
On March 20 last year, the March wheat contract jumped more than $2.00 a bushel minutes before the contract expired.

Media reports later surfaced of a CFTC Enforcement Division draft letter concerning three orders Arbor placed in the July 1996 wheat futures contract just after the close of trading in the expiring March contract.
The CBOT official said Arbor received the CFTC letter last month.
